mainTopic: The טבילה before entering the עזרה (חציצה, partial entry, the long knife), and the location of the כהן גדול's five טבילות, from which אביי calculates the height of עין עיטם
overview: This amud continues אביי's questions to רב יוסף about the טבילה needed before entering the עזרה. רב יוסף rules that whatever the רבנן enacted follows the Torah's model, so a חציצה invalidates even this rabbinic טבילה. He then proves from the מצורע, who immerses before putting his thumbs into the עזרה at שער ניקנור, that partial entry counts as entry. The גמרא asks whether someone standing outside who slaughters inside with a long knife needs טבילה. It works the question through בן זומא and through the רבנן who argue with רבי יהודה, and ends with תיקו. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's line about the כהן גדול's five טבילות and ten קידושין. A ברייתא teaches that all were in בית הפרוה except the first, which was on the roof of שער המים. From this אביי calculates that the spring עין עיטם was 23 אמות above the courtyard floor: a 20-אמה gate plus a מקוה 3 אמות deep.

steps.title: Does a barrier block this rabbinic immersion?
steps.stepSummary: אביי's question ends: does a חציצה invalidate this rabbinic טבילה or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it interpose, or does it not interpose?
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of אביי's question to רב יוסף. He asks whether a barrier on the body (חציצה) ruins this rabbinic טבילה before entering the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah-level טבילה is invalid if something blocks the water from touching the body. The doubt is whether a טבילה that the רבנן instituted, and that mainly serves as a reminder, is held to that same strict standard.

keyTerms.meaning: Interposes; acts as a barrier between the body and the water
A barrier that invalidates a טבילה
Immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: does it interpose, or does it not interpose?
phrases.notes: The end of a question that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun on the previous section of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the laws of חציצה apply to a rabbinic טבילה.

steps.title: Rabbinic enactments follow the Torah model
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that whatever the רבנן enacted, they modeled on Torah law, so a חציצה does invalidate.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Everything the רבנן instituted, they instituted similar to Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. Since the רבנן built their rules on the Torah's pattern, this טבילה has the same rules as a Torah טבילה, and a barrier invalidates it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a general principle, not a one-time ruling. When the רבנן create a requirement, they copy the basic structure of the Torah version. Here that means a rabbinic טבילה cannot be done with a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything the Sages instituted
Similar to Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון: rabbinic enactments follow the pattern of the Torah law they are modeled on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is used across ש״ס whenever the גמרא needs to decide how strict a rabbinic requirement is.

phrases.english: He said to him: Everything that the Sages instituted —
they instituted similar to Torah law.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חציצה invalidates the rabbinic טבילה, because rabbinic enactments mirror Torah law.

steps.title: Does partial entry count as entry?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether putting only part of the body into a place counts as entering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Is partial entry called entry or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question. If a person puts only part of his body into the עזרה, does that count as entering, so that he would need טבילה first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טבילה requirement is tied to entering the עזרה. The question is whether entry means the whole body, or whether even a partial entry triggers the requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Partial entry; entering with only part of the body
Is it called entry

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה בְּמִקְצָת, שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: partial entry — is it called entry or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same series about טבילה before entering the עזרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether partial entry into the עזרה counts as entry for the טבילה requirement.

steps.title: The מצורע's thumbs prove partial entry counts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves from the מצורע that partial entry counts: he immerses before putting his thumbs into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The thumbs will prove it, since they are partial entry. And a ברייתא taught: A מצורע immerses and stands at שער ניקנור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers with a proof. A מצורע puts his thumbs into the עזרה through שער ניקנור, which is only partial entry, and the ברייתא says he must immerse before standing there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע's body stays outside except for his thumbs. Even so, he immerses first. That shows partial entry is treated as entry for the טבילה requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Thumbs (and big toes) of the מצורע, which receive blood and oil
Will prove
A person with צרעת
The Nicanor Gate, the entrance to the עזרה
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He said to him: The thumbs will prove it,
since they are partial entry,
and it was taught: A leper immerses
and stands at the Gate of Nicanor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the partial-entry question by bringing proof from a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial entry counts as entry, as shown by the מצורע who immerses before putting his thumbs in.
steps.raayaObject: That partial entry counts as entry for the טבילה requirement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a מצורע immerses and stands at שער ניקנור.

steps.title: Slaughtering with a long knife from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone standing outside the עזרה who slaughters inside with a long knife needs טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A dilemma was raised to them: What is the law if he makes a long knife and slaughters?
steps.whatsHappening: A new dilemma is raised. A person stays fully outside the עזרה but slaughters an animal inside using a very long knife. Does he need טבילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: No part of his body enters, so even partial entry is not involved. The question isolates what actually triggers the טבילה requirement: physically entering, or doing the עבודה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A dilemma was raised before them
A long knife
And slaughter

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
what is the law if he makes a long knife and slaughters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes past partial entry to a case with no bodily entry at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether doing an עבודה from outside the עזרה requires טבילה.

steps.title: The dilemma applies to both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the question can be asked under both בן זומא and the רבנן who argue with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to בן זומא, and ask it according to the רבנן who disagree with רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces it will show why the question is open under each of two opinions, and the next two steps explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the question is not limited to one view. Each opinion has its own reason why the long-knife case could go either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Ask the question; the dilemma applies
The תנא who is stringent about this טבילה
Who disagree with him

phrases.english: Ask it according to Ben Zoma,

phrases.aramaic: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: ask it according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up how the dilemma plays out under each opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the long-knife question works under each of two opinions.

steps.title: The dilemma according to בן זומא
steps.stepSummary: Does בן זומא require טבילה only for one inside, or also for one outside, in case he gets drawn in?
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to בן זומא: Perhaps בן זומא obligates only one inside, but not one outside. Or perhaps he might be drawn in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the question under בן זומא. Maybe his requirement covers only someone inside the עזרה, or maybe it also covers someone outside, since he might be pulled inside while working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the requirement is about entering, so a person who stays outside is exempt. Side two: a protective concern that during the slaughter he will be drawn into the עזרה, so he should immerse anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Only up to here does he say; this is the limit of his ruling
For one inside
For one outside
Or perhaps
He may come to be drawn in

phrases.english: Ask it according to Ben Zoma:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא מְחַיֵּיב בֶּן זוֹמָא
phrases.english: Ben Zoma obligates only
one who is inside,
but one outside — no.
Or perhaps he may come to be drawn in.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּבְּעֵי לְבֶן זוֹמָא: עַד כָּאן לָא מְחַיֵּיב בֶּן זוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the first half of the setup in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בן זומא's טבילה requirement reaches someone standing outside, out of concern that he will be drawn in.

steps.title: The dilemma according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן exempt someone who does no עבודה; here he does עבודה, so maybe they require טבילה, or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the רבנן who disagree with רבי יהודה: Perhaps the רבנן exempt only there, where he does not perform service, but here, where he does perform service, they do not exempt. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the question under the רבנן. They exempt from טבילה someone who is not doing עבודה, and the question is whether they would still exempt someone who is doing עבודה from outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: what triggers the requirement is the עבודה, so slaughtering creates the obligation even from outside. Side two: the רבנן make no such distinction, and without entry there is no requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in the other case
Here, in our case
Performs the Temple service
There is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: Both repeated lines open with תיבעי and look like the setup in step 6. They are not a repetition. Steps 7 and 8 explain the reasoning behind each side of the question.

phrases.aramaic: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Ask it according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: The Rabbis said it only there,
where he is not performing service,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּקָא עָבֵיד עֲבוֹדָה — לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where he is performing service — no.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the second half of the setup in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן's exemption covers someone doing עבודה from outside the עזרה.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: תיקו: the long-knife dilemma is left unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. The question of slaughtering from outside with a long knife stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether entry or the עבודה itself triggers the טבילה, under either opinion. So the case remains undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Answered: a חציצה invalidates this rabbinic טבילה, and partial entry counts as entry (proven from the מצורע). Unanswered (תיקו): whether slaughtering from outside with a long knife requires טבילה.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dilemma without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether one who slaughters in the עזרה from outside with a long knife needs טבילה remains unresolved.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's line about five immersions and ten sanctifications
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to begin a new section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: The כהן גדול immerses five times and does ten sanctifications.
steps.whatsHappening: After finishing the long-knife question, the גמרא moves on and quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a heading line. It tells us which words of the משנה the גמרא will now explain. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול changes clothes five times, and each change needs one טבילה and two washings of hands and feet. That gives five טבילות and ten קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersing the whole body in a מקוה
Washing hands and feet from the כיור before and after עבודה
The High Priest

phrases.english: Five immersions and ten sanctifications he immerses.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה as a section heading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The long-knife discussion ended with תיקו in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום כיפור.

steps.title: ברייתא: all immersions in the holy area except the first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says all the טבילות were in בית הפרוה in the holy area, except the first, which was on the roof of שער המים in the non-holy area.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושין on that day. All of them are in the holy area, in בית הפרוה, except the first one. That one was in the non-holy area, on top of שער המים, next to his chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a detail the משנה did not give: where each טבילה took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the טבילות were inside the holy area of the עזרה, at בית הפרוה. The first one was different: it was in a non-holy area, on the roof of a gate called שער המים, near the כהן גדול's room. The fact that the מקוה was on a roof becomes the key point for אביי in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber in the עזרה where the כהן גדול immersed
Holy area, inside the עזרה
Non-holy area
The Water Gate, one of the gates of the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: The first טבילה is in חול because a person may not enter the עזרה at all without first immersing. That is why it cannot be done in the holy area like the others.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day,
and all of them are in the holy area, in the Hall of Parva,
except for the first, which was in the non-holy area
on top of the Water Gate,
and it was next to his chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה line by giving the location of each טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All טבילות were in בית הפרוה in the holy area, except the first, which was on the roof of שער המים in חול.

steps.title: אביי: עין עיטם was 23 cubits above the courtyard floor
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, אביי works out that the spring עין עיטם was 23 אמות higher than the floor of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that עין עיטם was 23 אמות higher than the floor of the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a surprising conclusion from the ברייתא about the height of the Temple's water source. The גמרא will now explain where the number 23 comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water flowed by itself from the spring עין עיטם into the מקוה on top of שער המים. Water only flows downhill, so the spring had to be higher than the water in that rooftop מקוה. אביי's number, 23, is built from two facts the גמרא brings next.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; a conclusion drawn from a source
The spring that supplied water to the בית המקדש
The floor of the Temple courtyard
Cubit, a unit of measurement

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
Ein Eitam was higher than the courtyard floor
by twenty-three cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's detail that the first טבילה was on the roof of שער המים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עין עיטם was 23 אמות higher than the floor of the עזרה.

steps.title: First source: the gates were 20 cubits tall
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that all the gates of the Temple were 20 אמות high, so the roof of שער המים was 20 אמות up.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: All the entrances there were 20 אמות high and 10 אמות wide, except the entrance of the אולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first piece of אביי's math: how high the gate was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every gate in the Temple, except the אולם, was 20 אמות tall. שער המים was a regular gate, so a מקוה on its roof sat 20 אמות above the courtyard floor. That gives the first 20 of the 23.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Entrances, gateways
The entrance hall of the היכל, whose opening was larger

phrases.english: As we learned: All the entrances that were there,
their height was twenty cubits
and their width ten cubits,
except for that of the Entrance Hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the first number behind אביי's 23.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that עין עיטם was 23 אמות high: the first 20 אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה stating that all Temple gates were 20 אמות high.

steps.title: Second source: a מקוה needs three cubits of water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא derives from the פסוק that a מקוה must hold enough water to cover the whole body: one אמה by one אמה, three אמות deep, which is 40 סאה. 20 + 3 = 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: 'And he shall wash his flesh in water' means in the water of a מקוה. 'All his flesh' means water that his whole body can enter. How much is that? One אמה by one אמה, three אמות high. The חכמים calculated that a מקוה holds 40 סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second piece of אביי's math: how deep the water in the rooftop מקוה had to be. This finishes the explanation of 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person's whole body must go into the water at once, a מקוה must be three אמות deep. The rooftop מקוה sat on a gate 20 אמות high and needed 3 more אמות of water. So the spring that filled it had to be at least 23 אמות above the courtyard floor.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
The water of a ritual bath
All his flesh: the whole body must be in the water at once
A measure of volume; a מקוה needs 40

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's 23 אמות = a 20-אמה-tall gate + 3 אמות of water depth for the rooftop מקוה. Water flows downhill, so the source spring had to be at least that high.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the basic size of a מקוה, 40 סאה, which is still the halachic standard.

phrases.english: And it was taught: 'And he shall wash his flesh in water'
means in the water of a ritual bath;

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל בְּשָׂרוֹ״ — מַיִם שֶׁכׇּל גּוּפוֹ עוֹלֶה בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: 'all his flesh' means water that his entire body can enter.
And how much is that?

phrases.aramaic: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: A cubit by a cubit, at a height of three cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים מֵי מִקְוֶה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה.
phrases.english: And the Sages calculated the water of a ritual bath at forty se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the 3 אמות of water depth to the 20-אמה gate height, completing the 23.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that עין עיטם was 23 אמות high: the last 3 אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא deriving from 'כׇּל בְּשָׂרוֹ' that a מקוה must be 1×1×3 אמות, which equals 40 סאה.
